items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names reveal intent and are used consistently (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookieAttribute, mergeConsistentHash, unionConsistentHash, applyConsistentHash). Every API field has a doc comment, and the wiring follows the existing plugin style.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: types are in traffic_policy_types.go, constructConsistentHash is in constructor.go, applyConsistentHash runs in handlePerRoutePolicies, and mergeConsistentHash is registered with SetOne/Append. Generated code came from go generate. consistent_hash.go stays under 500 lines.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: constructConsistentHash returns errors (e.g. for TTL parsing), which ConstructIR collects. A Validate method is registered. The CRD sets MinLength=1 on the key fields and has a CEL rule for disable. The p1-nil merge case uses clone() so IR state is not shared.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash is registered in MergeTrafficPolicies. It unions via unionConsistentHash with the correct priority order for each strategy, honours disable, and records the origin with mergeOrigins.SetOne/Append("consistentHash"). The hidden merge tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The CEL rule on ConsistentHash ("no other fields may be set when disable is true") appears in the CRD YAML and is covered by a validation test. When disable is set, the merge replaces the result with consistentHashIR{disable:true} and applying it produces no hash_policy. The default-to-sourceIp case passes the hidden tests.
